skill.name: biopython
skill.description: Use Biopython for sequence analysis, NCBI queries, BLAST workflows, file conversion, structure parsing, and phylogenetics in Python.
skill.summary: Work with molecular biology data in Python using Biopython examples and reference guides.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, biological identifiers, local file examples, and public documentation links. One real semantic risk remains: NCBI web BLAST and Entrez examples can transmit submitted sequence data to external services. No evidence of prompt injection or malicious command execution intent was found.

remediation.issue: External NCBI web requests may disclose sensitive sequence data.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear warning before NCBIWWW.qblast and Entrez examples. Recommend local BLAST or approved internal databases for confidential datasets.

remediation.issue: API key examples show literal placeholder assignment.
remediation.suggestion: Show loading NCBI API keys from environment variables or a user-managed secret store instead of assigning a string literal.

remediation.issue: Setup and search examples are easy for static scanners to misclassify.
remediation.suggestion: Label shell snippets as bash, keep Python snippets separate, and state that commands are optional setup or local documentation search.

semantic_findings.title: External NCBI Requests Can Expose Sequence Data
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs users to run NCBI web BLAST and Entrez workflows with supplied sequences and identifiers. Confidential, proprietary, or human-derived sequence data could leave the local environment if users follow these examples without approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples call NCBIWWW.qblast or describe NCBI web services with sequence inputs. This is legitimate bioinformatics functionality, but it creates a clear data-sharing boundary.

content.value_statement: Bioinformatics work often requires many file formats, public databases, and analysis modules. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical Biopython workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to create, inspect, translate, and transform DNA, RNA, and protein sequences.
Guides reading, writing, and converting FASTA, GenBank, FASTQ, PDB, mmCIF, and alignment files.
Shows how to query NCBI Entrez and PubMed with required email and rate-limit guidance.
Covers remote and local BLAST workflows, including result parsing and filtering.
Provides examples for protein structures, phylogenetic trees, motifs, and sequence statistics.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not include an executable wrapper or automated pipeline.
Remote NCBI examples may send submitted sequences or identifiers to external services.
Examples require Biopython, local input files, and any external tools named by the workflow.
It does not validate biological conclusions or replace expert review of analysis results.

use_cases.title: Convert sequence files
use_cases.description: Convert records between FASTA, GenBank, FASTQ, and related formats while preserving useful identifiers.

use_cases.title: Search public biology databases
use_cases.description: Build Entrez and PubMed queries, fetch records, and parse returned biological or publication data.

use_cases.title: Review comparative genomics results
use_cases.description: Parse BLAST output, inspect alignments, and prepare inputs for phylogenetic or structure analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Parse a FASTA file
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Biopython skill to show how I can read a FASTA file and summarize each sequence length and identifier.

prompt_templates.title: Convert biological formats
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Biopython skill to convert a GenBank file to FASTA and explain what metadata may be lost.

prompt_templates.title: Query NCBI responsibly
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Biopython skill to design an Entrez workflow that searches PubMed, fetches records, and respects NCBI requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Build a multi-step analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Biopython skill to plan a workflow that parses BLAST XML, filters hits, fetches top sequences, and prepares a phylogenetic tree.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to inspect a FASTA file with thousands of sequences.
output: A memory-efficient parsing approach using SeqIO iterators.
A summary of identifiers, sequence lengths, and filtering options.
Notes about testing on a small subset before processing the full file.

output_examples.input: A user needs to retrieve articles and sequence records from NCBI.
output: A clear Entrez search and fetch workflow.
A reminder to set the required email address and handle rate limits.
Guidance for caching downloaded records to avoid repeated requests.

output_examples.input: A user has BLAST XML and wants the strongest hits.
output: A parsing plan focused on E-value, identity, alignment length, and accession fields.
A recommendation to save parsed summaries separately from raw results.
Warnings about empty hits and privacy when using web BLAST.

best_practices: Use iterators for large files and test workflows on small datasets first.
Set required Entrez contact details and cache remote results to respect public services.
Record file formats, thresholds, database names, and software versions for reproducible analysis.
anti_patterns: Do not submit confidential sequence data to public web services without approval.
Do not load very large sequence files fully into memory when streaming is available.
Do not assume a parser format string is correct without validating sample input first.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps AI assistants use Biopython for molecular biology data handling and analysis tasks.

faq.question: Does it install Biopython automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation guidance, but the user or agent must run setup commands separately.

faq.question: Can it work with NCBI databases?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Entrez searches, record fetching, PubMed queries, and NCBI usage requirements.

faq.question: Can it parse BLAST results?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes workflows for BLAST XML, tabular output, filtering, and top-hit extraction.

faq.question: Is it safe for private sequence data?
faq.answer: Use local tools or approved internal services for confidential data. Public NCBI workflows can transmit submitted sequences.

faq.question: Does it replace scientific review?
faq.answer: No. It helps prepare and explain workflows, but domain experts should review methods and conclusions.
